To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of the Cbl cofactor-binding domain has been crystallized and preliminary data have been collected.
we have cloned, purified and characterized the cofactor-binding Cbl domain, which has been crystallized in the space group C2221 and diffracted to 3.1 Angstrom resolution.
the Cbl protein, which controls the expression of genes involved in sulfur assimilation, is a member of a large family of Lys-type transcriptional regulators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of the Lys R-type transcriptional regulator, Cbl, from Escherichiacoli.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for the function of Cbl in the control of sulfur assimilation in E. coli.
structural and functional characterization of the Lys-type transcriptional regulators and their role in regulation of gene expression in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the c-Cbl-APS complex crystallizes readily in a wide range of crystal forms and that the structure determination of the complex will be possible.
c-Cbl is a promising candidate for structure-function studies of LTTRs.
the crystal structure of the c-Cbl-APS complex will provide the structural basis of the regulatory mechanism of Cbl.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cbl has a novel structure and a novel function.
the structure of the Cbl-APS complex would be the first example of the LTTR-anti-inducer complex.
Cbl is the first member of the LTTR family for which structural studies are being performed in a complex with the putative anti-inducer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c-Cbl-APS complex can be successfully crystallized and that the structure will provide insight into the role of APS in the regulation of sulfur assimilation in E. coli.
the c-Cbl-APS complex crystallizes well in the absence of the DNA-binding domain.
